10-01.title: Jimmy Carter
10-01.description: 39th U.S. President who brokered the Camp David Accords and later won the Nobel Peace Prize for his humanitarian work.

10-01.title: Julie Andrews
10-01.description: British actress and singer who won the Oscar for Mary Poppins and became an icon through The Sound of Music.

10-01.title: Brie Larson
10-01.description: American actress who won the Oscar for Room and became the Marvel Cinematic Universe's Captain Marvel.

10-01.title: Walt Disney World Opens
10-01.description: Walt Disney World opened in Orlando, Florida, realizing Walt Disney's grander vision of a resort city built around a theme park.

10-01.title: China Celebrates National Day
10-01.description: Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the People's Republic of China in Tiananmen Square, establishing Communist rule.

10-01.title: "The Sound of Music" — Julie Andrews
10-01.description: Julie Andrews's joyful title song from the beloved Rodgers and Hammerstein musical film became one of the most recognizable melodies in history.

10-01.title: Room
10-01.description: Brie Larson won the Academy Award for her devastating performance as a mother raising her son in a tiny room where they are held captive.

10-02.title: Mahatma Gandhi
10-02.description: The father of the Indian independence movement who pioneered the philosophy of nonviolent civil disobedience that inspired the world.

10-02.title: Groucho Marx
10-02.description: American comedian, actor, and wit who led the Marx Brothers with rapid-fire wordplay and an irreverent style that defined modern comedy.

10-02.title: Sting
10-02.description: British musician, frontman of The Police, and solo artist whose eclectic songwriting spans rock, jazz, and classical.

10-02.title: International Day of Non-Violence Established
10-02.description: The UN established October 2 as the International Day of Non-Violence, marking Gandhi's birthday to promote his philosophy worldwide.

10-02.title: Thurgood Marshall Sworn In as Supreme Court Justice
10-02.description: Thurgood Marshall became the first African American Justice of the U.S. Supreme Court, a milestone in American legal history.

10-02.title: "Every Breath You Take" — The Police
10-02.description: Sting's deceptively romantic-sounding ode to obsessive surveillance became the biggest hit of 1983 and one of the most misunderstood songs ever.

10-02.title: Gandhi
10-02.description: Richard Attenborough's sweeping biopic starring Ben Kingsley as Mahatma Gandhi won eight Oscars including Best Picture.

10-03.title: Gwen Stefani
10-03.description: American singer-songwriter and fashion icon who fronted No Doubt and launched a successful solo career with 'Hollaback Girl.'

10-03.title: Neve Campbell
10-03.description: Canadian actress who became a scream queen as Sydney Prescott in the Scream franchise and starred in Party of Five.

10-03.title: Chubby Checker
10-03.description: American rock and roll singer whose recording of 'The Twist' launched a worldwide dance craze that is still performed today.

10-03.title: German Reunification
10-03.description: East and West Germany were officially reunified as the Federal Republic of Germany, ending four decades of Cold War division.

10-03.title: O.J. Simpson Acquitted
10-03.description: The not-guilty verdict in O.J. Simpson's murder trial brought the nation to a standstill and exposed deep racial divisions in America.

10-03.title: "Hollaback Girl" — Gwen Stefani
10-03.description: Gwen Stefani's abrasive, cheerleader-inspired pop single became the first digital download to sell one million copies in the U.S.

10-03.title: Scream
10-03.description: Wes Craven's meta horror film that both satirized and revived the slasher genre, launching one of horror's most beloved franchises.

10-04.title: Susan Sarandon
10-04.description: American actress and activist who won the Oscar for Dead Man Walking and starred in Thelma and Louise.

10-04.title: Alicia Silverstone
10-04.description: American actress who became the defining teen icon of the 1990s through Clueless and Aerosmith music videos.

10-04.title: Buster Keaton
10-04.description: American silent film comedian and director celebrated for deadpan performances and breathtaking physical comedy in The General.

10-04.title: Sputnik Launched — Space Age Begins
10-04.description: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik, Earth's first artificial satellite, triggering the Space Race and a new era of human civilization.

10-04.title: SpaceShipOne Wins Ansari X Prize
10-04.description: SpaceShipOne made its second spaceflight in five days to claim the $10 million Ansari X Prize, marking the dawn of private spaceflight.

10-04.title: "Crazy" — Aerosmith
10-04.description: Aerosmith's power ballad featuring Alicia Silverstone in the music video became one of the band's biggest hits of the 1990s.

10-04.title: Clueless
10-04.description: Amy Heckerling's sharp adaptation of Jane Austen's Emma, set in Beverly Hills high school, made Alicia Silverstone a generation's icon.

10-05.title: Kate Winslet
10-05.description: British actress who won the Oscar for The Reader and became a global icon playing Rose in Titanic.

10-05.title: Bob Geldof
10-05.description: Irish singer-songwriter who fronted the Boomtown Rats and organized Live Aid, the historic 1985 benefit concert that raised millions for famine relief.

10-05.title: Neil deGrasse Tyson
10-05.description: American astrophysicist and science communicator who made the cosmos accessible to millions through Cosmos: A Spacetime Odyssey.

10-05.title: Steve Jobs Dies
10-05.description: Apple co-founder Steve Jobs died at 56 from pancreatic cancer, prompting an outpouring of grief from around the world.

10-05.title: The Beatles Release 'Love Me Do'
10-05.description: The Beatles released their debut single 'Love Me Do' on EMI's Parlophone label, beginning the most successful recording career in history.

10-05.title: "I Don't Want to Miss a Thing" — Aerosmith
10-05.description: Written for the Armageddon soundtrack, this soaring Aerosmith ballad became the band's only No. 1 single in the U.S.

10-05.title: Titanic
10-05.description: James Cameron's sweeping romance aboard the doomed ocean liner starred Leonardo DiCaprio and Kate Winslet and became the highest-grossing film of its time.

10-06.title: Hafez al-Assad
10-06.description: Syrian president who ruled for three decades with an iron fist and transformed Syria into a Ba'athist one-party state.

10-06.title: Elisabeth Shue
10-06.description: American actress nominated for the Oscar for Leaving Las Vegas who also starred in Back to the Future II and III.

10-06.title: Ioan Gruffudd
10-06.description: Welsh actor known for playing Horatio Hornblower on TV and Reed Richards in the Fantastic Four films.

10-06.title: The Jazz Singer — First Sound Film
10-06.description: The Jazz Singer premiered, becoming the first feature-length film with synchronized dialogue and marking the end of the silent film era.

10-06.title: Yom Kippur War Begins
10-06.description: Egypt and Syria launched a surprise attack on Israel on the holiest day of the Jewish calendar, triggering the 1973 Arab-Israeli War.

10-06.title: "Superstition" — Stevie Wonder
10-06.description: Stevie Wonder's funky, clavinet-driven masterpiece was written for Jeff Beck but became one of Wonder's most beloved recordings.

10-06.title: The Departed
10-06.description: Martin Scorsese's layered crime thriller about police infiltrating the mob and vice versa finally won him the Academy Award for Best Director.

10-07.title: Thom Yorke
10-07.description: British musician and lead vocalist of Radiohead whose experimental approach to rock music has influenced a generation of artists.

10-07.title: Yo-Yo Ma
10-07.description: French-American cellist of Chinese heritage who is widely regarded as the greatest living classical musician.

10-07.title: Simon Cowell
10-07.description: British TV personality and music executive who built a reality TV empire through American Idol, X Factor, and Britain's Got Talent.

10-07.title: U.S. Invades Afghanistan
10-07.description: The United States launched Operation Enduring Freedom, beginning its military campaign in Afghanistan in response to the September 11 attacks.

10-07.title: Vladimir Putin Becomes Prime Minister
10-07.description: Boris Yeltsin appointed Vladimir Putin as Prime Minister of Russia, beginning Putin's two-decade dominance of Russian politics.

10-07.title: OK Computer — Radiohead
10-07.description: Radiohead's landmark album, blending paranoid lyrics with sweeping orchestral rock, is frequently cited as the greatest album of the 1990s.

10-07.title: You've Got Mail
10-07.description: Nora Ephron's internet-age romantic comedy starring Tom Hanks and Meg Ryan captured the early magic of online connection.

10-08.title: Chevy Chase
10-08.description: American comedian and original Saturday Night Live cast member known for his pratfalls and the National Lampoon's Vacation films.

10-08.title: Matt Damon
10-08.description: American actor and screenwriter who won the Oscar for Good Will Hunting and became an action star through the Bourne franchise.

10-08.title: Bruno Mars
10-08.description: Hawaiian-American pop and R&B artist renowned for his retro musical style and electrifying live performances.

10-08.title: Great Chicago Fire Begins
10-08.description: A fire broke out near the O'Leary barn in Chicago and burned for two days, destroying 3.3 square miles of the city.

10-08.title: Black Monday Stock Market Crash
10-08.description: Stock markets around the world crashed on Black Monday with the Dow Jones losing 22.6% of its value in a single day.

10-08.title: "Uptown Funk" — Mark Ronson ft. Bruno Mars
10-08.description: This retro funk banger spent a record-tying 14 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and became one of the best-selling singles ever.

10-08.title: Good Will Hunting
10-08.description: Matt Damon and Ben Affleck's Oscar-winning screenplay about a mathematical genius from South Boston launched two of Hollywood's biggest careers.

10-09.title: John Lennon
10-09.description: Founding member of The Beatles whose songwriting partnership with Paul McCartney produced the most celebrated body of work in rock history.

10-09.title: Che Guevara
10-09.description: Argentine Marxist revolutionary executed in Bolivia in 1967, whose iconic portrait became the most reproduced image in photography history.

10-09.title: Sharon Osbourne
10-09.description: British TV personality and music manager who guided Ozzy Osbourne's career and became a beloved panelist on The Talk and The X Factor.

10-09.title: East Germany Founded
10-09.description: The German Democratic Republic was proclaimed in East Berlin, completing the division of Germany into two separate states.

10-09.title: Leif Erikson Day
10-09.description: Commemorating the Norse explorer Leif Erikson who reached North America around 1000 AD — nearly 500 years before Columbus.

10-09.title: "Imagine" — John Lennon
10-09.description: John Lennon's ethereal hymn to peace and unity became one of the most covered and recognized songs in the history of popular music.

10-09.title: Nowhere Boy
10-09.description: Sam Taylor-Johnson's biopic dramatized John Lennon's teenage years in Liverpool before the formation of The Beatles.

10-10.title: Giuseppe Verdi
10-10.description: Italian opera composer whose works — including Rigoletto, La Traviata, and Aida — are the bedrock of the operatic repertoire.

10-10.title: David Lee Roth
10-10.description: American rock singer and frontman of Van Halen who defined glam metal showmanship with unmatched stage energy.

10-10.title: Dale Earnhardt Jr.
10-10.description: American NASCAR driver and son of legend Dale Earnhardt Sr. who became NASCAR's most popular driver for 15 consecutive years.

10-10.title: Spiro Agnew Resigns as Vice President
10-10.description: Vice President Spiro Agnew resigned and pleaded no contest to tax evasion charges, the second VP ever to resign from office.

10-10.title: World Mental Health Day Established
10-10.description: The World Federation for Mental Health established October 10 as World Mental Health Day to raise awareness of mental health issues globally.

10-10.title: "Jump" — Van Halen
10-10.description: Van Halen's unlikely synthesizer-driven No. 1 hit opened their landmark 1984 album and became one of the decade's defining rock songs.

10-10.title: 10 Things I Hate About You
10-10.description: This modern adaptation of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew starring Julia Stiles and Heath Ledger became the definitive 1990s teen rom-com.

10-11.title: Eleanor Roosevelt
10-11.description: American diplomat and humanitarian who transformed the role of First Lady and became a driving force behind the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

10-11.title: Luke Perry
10-11.description: American actor who became a teen idol as Dylan McKay on Beverly Hills 90210 before earning critical acclaim in Once Upon a Time in Hollywood.

10-11.title: Joan Cusack
10-11.description: American actress and twice Oscar-nominated comedian known for Working Girl and her recurring role in the Toy Story franchise.

10-11.title: Vatican II Opens
10-11.description: Pope John XXIII opened the Second Vatican Council, the most significant Catholic Church reform in centuries, modernizing liturgy and theology.

10-11.title: Saturday Night Live Premieres
10-11.description: NBC's Saturday Night Live debuted with George Carlin as host, launching the most influential late-night comedy show in television history.

10-11.title: "Mrs. Robinson" — Simon and Garfunkel
10-11.description: Written for The Graduate's soundtrack, Simon and Garfunkel's wry character study became one of the 1960s' most celebrated songs.

10-11.title: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood
10-11.description: Quentin Tarantino's nostalgic love letter to 1969 Hollywood starred Leonardo DiCaprio, Brad Pitt, and a brief, luminous Luke Perry.

10-12.title: Luciano Pavarotti
10-12.description: Italian operatic tenor widely regarded as the greatest of the 20th century, who brought opera to stadiums and sold over 100 million records.

10-12.title: Hugh Jackman
10-12.description: Australian actor who defined Wolverine for an entire generation across nine Marvel films while also earning Tony and Grammy nominations.

10-12.title: Aleister Crowley
10-12.description: British occultist and founder of Thelema whose provocative persona as 'The Great Beast' made him one of the most controversial figures of the 20th century.

10-12.title: Columbus Reaches the Americas
10-12.description: Christopher Columbus made landfall on an island in the Bahamas, beginning the European encounter with the Americas.

10-12.title: USS Cole Bombing
10-12.description: Al-Qaeda terrorists attacked the U.S. Navy destroyer USS Cole in Yemen's Aden harbor, killing 17 American sailors.

10-12.title: "Nessun Dorma" — Luciano Pavarotti
10-12.description: Pavarotti's electrifying performance of Puccini's aria at the 1990 World Cup became the most famous classical performance of modern times.

10-12.title: X2: X-Men United
10-12.description: The acclaimed sequel featuring Hugh Jackman's Wolverine at his most ferocious is considered one of the best superhero films ever made.

10-13.title: Margaret Thatcher
10-13.description: Britain's first female Prime Minister, the Iron Lady whose free-market policies reshaped British society through the 1980s.

10-13.title: Paul Simon
10-13.description: American singer-songwriter who with Art Garfunkel created folk-rock landmarks like The Sound of Silence before his solo triumph Graceland.

10-13.title: Sacha Baron Cohen
10-13.description: British comedian who created boundary-pushing characters Borat, Ali G, and Bruno to expose prejudice through outrageous provocations.

10-13.title: Chilean Miners Rescued
10-13.description: All 33 miners trapped underground for 69 days in the Copiapó mining disaster were rescued to worldwide jubilation.

10-13.title: King Bhumibol Adulyadej Dies
10-13.description: Thailand's King Bhumibol Adulyadej died after 70 years on the throne — the longest reign of any monarch in the world.

10-13.title: Graceland — Paul Simon
10-13.description: Paul Simon's groundbreaking album blending American rock with South African township music won the Grammy for Album of the Year.

10-13.title: The 33
10-13.description: Antonio Banderas led the cast in this dramatization of the miraculous 2010 Chilean mining rescue that captivated the world.

10-14.title: Dwight D. Eisenhower
10-14.description: Supreme Commander of Allied Forces in WWII and 34th U.S. President who oversaw the D-Day invasion and the postwar economic boom.

10-14.title: Usher
10-14.description: American R&B superstar who defined the early 2000s with the diamond-certified album Confessions and his electrifying dance moves.

10-14.title: Roger Moore
10-14.description: British actor who played James Bond seven times and brought a lighter, more comedic touch to the role than any other 007.

10-14.title: Chuck Yeager Breaks the Sound Barrier
10-14.description: Test pilot Chuck Yeager became the first person to fly faster than the speed of sound in the Bell X-1 aircraft over California.

10-14.title: Martin Luther King Jr. Wins Nobel Peace Prize
10-14.description: Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize at age 35, becoming the youngest person to receive the honor at the time.

10-14.title: Confessions — Usher
10-14.description: Usher's fourth studio album became one of the best-selling albums of the 2000s with four No. 1 singles including 'Yeah!' and 'Burn.'

10-14.title: The Right Stuff
10-14.description: Philip Kaufman's epic film about the early days of the U.S. space program opens with Chuck Yeager's historic supersonic flight.

10-15.title: Friedrich Nietzsche
10-15.description: German philosopher who declared 'God is dead' and whose concepts of the will to power and eternal recurrence profoundly shaped modern thought.

10-15.title: Emeril Lagasse
10-15.description: American celebrity chef and restaurateur who made cooking entertaining TV with his energetic 'Bam!' catchphrase.

10-15.title: Tanya Tucker
10-15.description: American country music singer who scored her first hit at age 13 with 'Delta Dawn' and became a country institution.

10-15.title: Mata Hari Executed
10-15.description: Dutch exotic dancer and alleged double agent Mata Hari was executed by firing squad in France, becoming history's most famous spy.

10-15.title: Vietnam Moratorium Anti-War Demonstration
10-15.description: The Vietnam Moratorium, the largest single-day anti-war demonstration in U.S. history, drew millions of protesters across America.

10-15.title: "Space Oddity" — David Bowie
10-15.description: Released days before the Apollo 11 moon landing, Bowie's tale of Major Tom drifting alone in space became his first major hit.

10-15.title: Apocalypse Now
10-15.description: Francis Ford Coppola's hallucinatory journey up the Mekong Delta is widely regarded as the definitive film about the Vietnam War.

10-16.title: Oscar Wilde
10-16.description: Irish poet and playwright whose wit and flamboyance defined an era, producing masterworks like The Importance of Being Earnest and The Picture of Dorian Gray.

10-16.title: Eugene O'Neill
10-16.description: American playwright and Nobel laureate who brought raw, psychological realism to the stage with Long Day's Journey into Night and Mourning Becomes Electra.

10-16.title: John Mayer
10-16.description: Grammy-winning American singer-guitarist who moved from coffeehouse pop to blues-rock virtuosity and became one of the most skilled guitarists of his generation.

10-16.title: Cuban Missile Crisis Begins
10-16.description: President Kennedy was briefed on Soviet nuclear missiles in Cuba, triggering the most dangerous thirteen days of the Cold War.

10-16.title: China Tests Its First Nuclear Weapon
10-16.description: China detonated its first atomic bomb, becoming the fifth nuclear power in the world and shifting the balance of the Cold War.

10-16.title: Continuum — John Mayer
10-16.description: John Mayer's blues-infused third album earned three Grammy Awards and is considered his defining artistic statement.

10-16.title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
10-16.description: Albert Lewin's stylish adaptation of Oscar Wilde's only novel follows a beautiful young man whose portrait ages in his place as he descends into sin.

10-17.title: Eminem
10-17.description: Detroit rapper who became one of the best-selling music artists in history, reshaping hip-hop with his ferocious wordplay and alter ego Slim Shady.

10-17.title: Rita Hayworth
10-17.description: Hollywood's 'Love Goddess' who became the definitive pin-up of World War II and dazzled in Gilda and Cover Girl.

10-17.title: Arthur Miller
10-17.description: American playwright whose Death of a Salesman and The Crucible stand as two of the most powerful dramas of the 20th century.

10-17.title: Loma Prieta Earthquake Strikes San Francisco
10-17.description: A 6.9-magnitude earthquake struck the San Francisco Bay Area moments before Game 3 of the World Series, killing 63 people.

10-17.title: Al Capone Convicted of Tax Evasion
10-17.description: Notorious Chicago mob boss Al Capone was found guilty of tax evasion, ending his criminal empire after the government succeeded where police could not.

10-17.title: The Marshall Mathers LP — Eminem
10-17.description: Eminem's third album sold a then-record 1.76 million copies in its first week and remains one of the fastest-selling rap albums in history.

10-17.title: 8 Mile
10-17.description: Curtis Hanson's semi-autobiographical drama starring Eminem as a Detroit rapper scrapping his way out of poverty won the Oscar for Best Original Song.

10-18.title: Chuck Berry
10-18.description: Rock and roll pioneer whose guitar riffs, showmanship, and songs like 'Johnny B. Goode' laid the blueprint for virtually every rock band that followed.

10-18.title: Martina Navratilova
10-18.description: Czech-American tennis legend who won a record nine Wimbledon singles titles and 167 career singles titles, dominating the sport through the 1980s.

10-18.title: Pierre Trudeau
10-18.description: Canada's 15th Prime Minister who shaped modern Canada with the Charter of Rights and Freedoms and his charismatic, intellectual style.

10-18.title: Alaska Formally Transferred to United States
10-18.description: The United States formally took possession of Alaska from Russia in a ceremony at Sitka, completing a purchase of 586,000 square miles for $7.2 million.

10-18.title: First All-Female NASA Spacewalk
10-18.description: Astronauts Christina Koch and Jessica Meir conducted the first all-female spacewalk in history outside the International Space Station.

10-18.title: "Johnny B. Goode" — Chuck Berry
10-18.description: Chuck Berry's electrifying ode to a guitar-playing country boy became the defining rock and roll song and was sent into space on the Voyager Golden Record.

10-18.title: Back to the Future
10-18.description: Robert Zemeckis's time-travel comedy featuring Marty McFly's guitar hero moment at the Enchantment Under the Sea dance is one of the most beloved films ever made.

10-19.title: John Lithgow
10-19.description: American actor with extraordinary range who won Emmys for 3rd Rock from the Sun, a Tony for Dirty Rotten Scoundrels, and critical praise for The Crown.

10-19.title: Jon Favreau
10-19.description: American filmmaker who directed the first Iron Man, effectively launching the Marvel Cinematic Universe and changing Hollywood blockbuster culture forever.

10-19.title: Evander Holyfield
10-19.description: American professional boxer and the only four-time world heavyweight champion, whose bouts with Mike Tyson produced two of boxing's most iconic moments.

10-19.title: Cornwallis Surrenders at Yorktown
10-19.description: British General Cornwallis surrendered to George Washington at Yorktown, Virginia, effectively ending the American Revolutionary War.

10-19.title: Saddam Hussein Goes on Trial
10-19.description: Former Iraqi president Saddam Hussein was tried for crimes against humanity, beginning a legal process that ended with his execution in 2006.

10-19.title: Iron Man Soundtrack — Ramin Djawadi
10-19.description: Ramin Djawadi's score for Jon Favreau's Iron Man set the muscular, AC/DC-infused tone that defined the sound of the entire Marvel Cinematic Universe.

10-19.title: Iron Man
10-19.description: Jon Favreau's film starring Robert Downey Jr. as Tony Stark launched the most financially successful cinematic franchise in Hollywood history.

10-20.title: Tom Petty
10-20.description: American rock legend whose anthemic heartland songs with Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers made him one of the most beloved artists in rock history.

10-20.title: Snoop Dogg
10-20.description: Iconic Long Beach rapper who emerged under Dr. Dre's wing and became one of the most recognizable cultural figures in hip-hop history.

10-20.title: Danny Boyle
10-20.description: British director whose kinetic visual style produced genre-defying films from Trainspotting and 28 Days Later to the Oscar-winning Slumdog Millionaire.

10-20.title: Sydney Opera House Opens
10-20.description: Queen Elizabeth II officially opened the Sydney Opera House, one of the 20th century's most iconic architectural achievements.

10-20.title: Watergate Saturday Night Massacre
10-20.description: President Nixon ordered the firing of special prosecutor Archibald Cox, triggering a constitutional crisis and accelerating Nixon's downfall.

10-20.title: "Free Fallin'" — Tom Petty
10-20.description: Tom Petty's easy, wistful ode to Los Angeles became one of the defining songs of the 1980s and one of rock's most beloved singalongs.

10-20.title: Slumdog Millionaire
10-20.description: Danny Boyle's kinetic rags-to-riches story set in Mumbai swept the Oscars, winning eight awards including Best Picture and Best Director.

10-21.title: Carrie Fisher
10-21.description: American actress, writer, and advocate who immortalized Princess Leia in Star Wars and became a vital voice for mental health awareness.

10-21.title: Celia Cruz
10-21.description: The undisputed Queen of Salsa, Cuba's greatest musical export who sang with unrivaled power and joy for over five decades.

10-21.title: Kim Kardashian
10-21.description: American media personality and businesswoman who turned reality TV fame into a billion-dollar beauty empire and became a defining celebrity of the social media age.

10-21.title: Magellan Discovers the Strait of Magellan
10-21.description: Ferdinand Magellan's fleet entered the passage at the southern tip of South America that would bear his name, opening a westward route to the Pacific.

10-21.title: Battle of Trafalgar
10-21.description: Admiral Horatio Nelson led the British fleet to a decisive victory over Napoleon's navy off the coast of Spain, though Nelson died in the battle.

10-21.title: "Quimbara" — Celia Cruz
10-21.description: Celia Cruz's explosive salsa anthem with the Fania All Stars became her signature song and a touchstone of Latin music culture.

10-21.title: Star Wars: The Force Awakens
10-21.description: The long-awaited sequel to the original trilogy reunited Carrie Fisher's Princess Leia with Han Solo and Luke Skywalker for a new generation.

10-22.title: Franz Liszt
10-22.description: Hungarian composer and pianist widely considered the greatest keyboard virtuoso in history, who essentially invented the modern solo piano recital.

10-22.title: Jeff Goldblum
10-22.description: American actor celebrated for his magnetic, idiosyncratic presence in Jurassic Park, The Fly, and The Grand Budapest Hotel.

10-22.title: Christopher Lloyd
10-22.description: American character actor best known for his iconic portrayal of the eccentric inventor Doc Brown in the Back to the Future trilogy.

10-22.title: Thomas Edison Tests First Practical Light Bulb
10-22.description: Thomas Edison successfully tested an incandescent light bulb with a carbonized thread filament that burned for 13.5 hours, changing civilization forever.

10-22.title: International Meridian Conference Establishes Prime Meridian
10-22.description: The International Meridian Conference designated the Royal Observatory at Greenwich as the world's prime meridian, standardizing global navigation.

10-22.title: Hungarian Rhapsody No. 2 — Franz Liszt
10-22.description: Liszt's dazzling showpiece for solo piano became one of the most famous concert works ever written, later immortalized in cartoons and films.

10-22.title: Jurassic Park
10-22.description: Steven Spielberg's dinosaur thriller starred Jeff Goldblum as the chaos theorist whose warnings go unheeded, revolutionizing CGI in cinema.

10-23.title: Pelé
10-23.description: Brazilian football legend widely regarded as the greatest player in the history of the sport, who won three FIFA World Cups and scored over 1,000 goals.

10-23.title: Johnny Carson
10-23.description: King of late-night television who hosted The Tonight Show for 30 years and made it the gold standard of American talk show entertainment.

10-23.title: Ryan Reynolds
10-23.description: Canadian actor and comedian who parlayed his sharp wit into a billion-dollar career, most famously playing the motor-mouthed antihero Deadpool.

10-23.title: First National Women's Rights Convention
10-23.description: The first National Women's Rights Convention in Worcester, Massachusetts drew hundreds of delegates and launched organized suffrage activism in the United States.

10-23.title: Beirut Barracks Bombing
10-23.description: Simultaneous suicide truck bombings killed 241 American and 58 French peacekeepers in Beirut, the deadliest single-day toll for the U.S. Marine Corps since Iwo Jima.

10-23.title: "Weird Al" Yankovic — In 3-D
10-23.description: Weird Al Yankovic's breakthrough album — sharing a birthday with October 23 — contained his Michael Jackson parody 'Eat It,' which reached No. 12.

10-23.title: Deadpool
10-23.description: Ryan Reynolds' passion project defied Hollywood wisdom to become the highest-grossing R-rated film ever made at the time of its release.

10-24.title: Drake
10-24.description: Toronto rapper and R&B artist who became the most-streamed artist in Spotify history, dominating pop culture with his emotionally candid style.

10-24.title: Kevin Kline
10-24.description: Tony and Oscar-winning American actor known for his swashbuckling comic performances in A Fish Called Wanda and Sophie's Choice.

10-24.title: Wayne Rooney
10-24.description: English football legend and Manchester United's all-time leading scorer who became one of the most dominant forwards of his era.

10-24.title: First Transcontinental Telegraph Completed
10-24.description: The first transcontinental telegraph line linking San Francisco to Washington, D.C. was completed, making the Pony Express immediately obsolete.

10-24.title: Concorde Makes Its Last Commercial Flight
10-24.description: The supersonic Concorde made its final passenger flight, ending an era of transatlantic travel at twice the speed of sound.

10-24.title: Take Care — Drake
10-24.description: Drake's second studio album fused rap and R&B into a moody, introspective masterpiece that won the Grammy for Best Rap Album.

10-24.title: A Fish Called Wanda
10-24.description: Kevin Kline's Oscar-winning anarchic performance as the dim-witted Texan thief in this British heist comedy is one of the funniest in film history.

10-25.title: Pablo Picasso
10-25.description: Spanish painter and sculptor who co-founded Cubism, shattered conventions of representation, and produced one of the most prolific bodies of work in art history.

10-25.title: Katy Perry
10-25.description: American pop superstar who became the first artist to spend 69 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and captivated the world with her colorful, bold aesthetic.

10-25.title: Helen Reddy
10-25.description: Australian-American singer whose 1972 hit 'I Am Woman' became the defining anthem of second-wave feminism and the women's liberation movement.

10-25.title: Battle of Agincourt
10-25.description: Henry V's vastly outnumbered English army defeated the French at Agincourt in one of history's most celebrated military victories, immortalized by Shakespeare.

10-25.title: Hungary Declares Itself a Republic
10-25.description: Hungary officially declared itself a democratic republic, abandoning communism and marking one of the pivotal moments in the fall of the Soviet bloc.

10-25.title: "I Am Woman" — Helen Reddy
10-25.description: Helen Reddy's soaring declaration of female empowerment topped the charts and became the theme song of the women's liberation movement worldwide.

10-25.title: Surviving Picasso
10-25.description: James Ivory's film starring Anthony Hopkins as Pablo Picasso explored the legendary artist's tumultuous relationships through the eyes of his muse Françoise Gilot.

10-26.title: Hillary Clinton
10-26.description: American politician who served as First Lady, U.S. Senator, Secretary of State, and became the first woman nominated for President by a major party.

10-26.title: Mahalia Jackson
10-26.description: The 'Queen of Gospel' whose thunderous contralto made her the most celebrated gospel singer of the 20th century and a pillar of the Civil Rights Movement.

10-26.title: Jaclyn Smith
10-26.description: American actress who became a global icon as Kelly Garrett in Charlie's Angels and later built a successful fashion and beauty business.

10-26.title: Charles V Crowned Holy Roman Emperor
10-26.description: Charles V was crowned Holy Roman Emperor at Aachen, beginning the reign of the most powerful ruler in Europe at the height of the Renaissance.

10-26.title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas Released
10-26.description: Rockstar Games released Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas for PlayStation 2, which became the console's best-selling game ever with 17 million copies sold.

10-26.title: "How I Got Over" — Mahalia Jackson
10-26.description: Mahalia Jackson's gospel signature captured her raw spiritual power and became one of the foundational recordings of American sacred music.

10-26.title: Charlie's Angels
10-26.description: McG's high-energy adaptation of the classic TV series updated Jaclyn Smith's era with a new trio of action heroines for the millennial generation.

10-27.title: Theodore Roosevelt
10-27.description: 26th U.S. President, Nobel Peace Prize laureate, and conservationist who established the national park system and busted industrial monopolies.

10-27.title: Sylvia Plath
10-27.description: American confessional poet and author of The Bell Jar whose intensely personal verse and tragic life made her one of the most influential literary voices of the 20th century.

10-27.title: John Cleese
10-27.description: British comedian and co-founder of Monty Python whose absurdist sketches, including the Ministry of Silly Walks, became comedy's gold standard.

10-27.title: New York City Subway Opens
10-27.description: New York City's subway system opened with its first line running from City Hall to 145th Street, beginning one of the world's great transit systems.

10-27.title: Lynyrd Skynyrd Plane Crash
10-27.description: A plane crash in Mississippi killed Lynyrd Skynyrd frontman Ronnie Van Zant and two other bandmates, abruptly ending one of Southern rock's greatest acts.

10-27.title: "Sweet Home Alabama" — Lynyrd Skynyrd
10-27.description: Lynyrd Skynyrd's swaggering Southern rock anthem remains one of the most recognizable and beloved guitar riffs in rock and roll history.

10-27.title: Monty Python and the Holy Grail
10-27.description: John Cleese and the Monty Python troupe created the funniest film about medieval chivalry ever made, a comedy so quotable it entered the cultural lexicon.

10-28.title: Bill Gates
10-28.description: Co-founder of Microsoft who turned a small software company into the most valuable corporation in history and later became one of the world's great philanthropists.

10-28.title: Julia Roberts
10-28.description: American actress whose megawatt smile and magnetic charm made her Hollywood's highest-paid actress through Pretty Woman, Erin Brockovich, and Ocean's Eleven.

10-28.title: Jonas Salk
10-28.description: American virologist who developed the first safe and effective polio vaccine in 1955, and then refused to patent it, saying it belonged to the people.

10-28.title: Statue of Liberty Dedicated
10-28.description: President Grover Cleveland dedicated the Statue of Liberty in New York Harbor, a gift from France that became America's defining symbol of freedom.

10-28.title: Tchaikovsky Premieres His Final Symphony
10-28.description: Pyotr Tchaikovsky conducted the world premiere of his Pathétique Symphony in St. Petersburg, just nine days before his mysterious death.

10-28.title: "Pretty Woman" — Roy Orbison
10-28.description: Roy Orbison's explosive rock ballad, later immortalized by Julia Roberts's film, is one of the most instantly recognizable opening guitar riffs in pop history.

10-28.title: Pretty Woman
10-28.description: Garry Marshall's Cinderella story starring Julia Roberts and Richard Gere became one of the highest-grossing romantic comedies of all time.

10-29.title: Winona Ryder
10-29.description: American actress who defined Generation X cool with Beetlejuice, Edward Scissorhands, and Reality Bites before her acclaimed comeback in Stranger Things.

10-29.title: Richard Dreyfuss
10-29.description: American actor who became a New Hollywood icon through Jaws, Close Encounters of the Third Kind, and won the Oscar for The Goodbye Girl.

10-29.title: Gabrielle Union
10-29.description: American actress and activist who broke through with Bring It On and has become an outspoken advocate for survivors of sexual violence.

10-29.title: Black Tuesday — Stock Market Crash of 1929
10-29.description: The New York Stock Exchange collapsed on Black Tuesday as investors traded 16 million shares in panic, wiping out fortunes and triggering the Great Depression.

10-29.title: ARPANET Sends First Message
10-29.description: The first message was transmitted over ARPANET between UCLA and Stanford, a simple 'LO' before the system crashed — the humble birth of the internet.

10-29.title: "Beetlejuice" Theme — Danny Elfman
10-29.description: Danny Elfman's quirky, calypso-inflected score for Tim Burton's Beetlejuice established the composer-director partnership that would define dark fantasy cinema.

10-29.title: Beetlejuice
10-29.description: Tim Burton's anarchic supernatural comedy starring Winona Ryder as a goth teenager unleashed Michael Keaton's most outrageously funny performance.

10-30.title: John Adams
10-30.description: Founding Father, key architect of American independence, and second U.S. President who helped draft the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution.

10-30.title: Ezra Pound
10-30.description: Radical American modernist poet whose Cantos and editorial mentorship shaped 20th-century literature, helping launch the careers of T.S. Eliot and James Joyce.

10-30.title: Diego Maradona
10-30.description: Argentine football deity who scored the 'Hand of God' goal and the 'Goal of the Century' in the same match, leading Argentina to the 1986 World Cup.

10-30.title: War of the Worlds Radio Broadcast Panics America
10-30.description: Orson Welles' dramatic radio adaptation of H.G. Wells' Martian invasion story caused widespread panic among listeners who believed the broadcast was real.

10-30.title: Muhammad Ali Wins the Rumble in the Jungle
10-30.description: Muhammad Ali reclaimed the heavyweight title by knocking out George Foreman in Kinshasa with his legendary 'rope-a-dope' strategy.

10-30.title: When Doves Cry — Prince
10-30.description: Prince's drumless, bass-free funk masterpiece spent five weeks at No. 1 and became the biggest U.S. hit of 1984, extracted from his Purple Rain album.

10-30.title: When We Were Kings
10-30.description: Leon Gast's Oscar-winning documentary captured Muhammad Ali's legendary Rumble in the Jungle match and the cultural spectacle surrounding it in Zaire.

10-31.title: Peter Jackson
10-31.description: New Zealand director who turned J.R.R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings into a landmark film trilogy, winning 11 Oscars including Best Picture for The Return of the King.

10-31.title: John Keats
10-31.description: English Romantic poet who produced an extraordinary body of work before dying at 25, leaving odes to autumn and a nightingale that still resonate centuries later.

10-31.title: Michael Landon
10-31.description: American actor, director, and producer who became a beloved television institution through Bonanza, Little House on the Prairie, and Highway to Heaven.

10-31.title: Martin Luther Posts the Ninety-Five Theses
10-31.description: Martin Luther nailed his protest against papal corruption to the door of Wittenberg's Castle Church, igniting the Protestant Reformation that split Christendom.

10-31.title: Mount Rushmore Completed
10-31.description: After 14 years of carving, the Mount Rushmore National Memorial was declared complete, featuring the faces of four U.S. presidents in the Black Hills of South Dakota.

10-31.title: Thriller — Michael Jackson
10-31.description: Michael Jackson's Halloween-flavored title track from the best-selling album of all time features Vincent Price's iconic spoken-word outro and a legendary zombie music video.

10-31.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
10-31.description: Peter Jackson's epic finale swept the Oscars with 11 wins including Best Picture, tying the all-time record and cementing his trilogy as cinema's greatest fantasy achievement.
